definitions.gloss: covered in ~; full of ~; riddled with ~
definitions.explanation: Attaches to nouns to indicate being covered in or full of something undesirable. Almost always carries a negative connotation. Functions as a no-adjective when modifying nouns.

examples.english: My hands are covered in mud.

examples.japanese: このレポートは{間違|まちが}いだらけで{出|だ}せない。
examples.english: This report is full of mistakes, so I can't submit it.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}んで{帰|かえ}ってきた{子供|こども}は、{服|ふく}が{砂|すな}だらけになっていた。
examples.english: The child who came back from playing in the park had clothes covered in sand.

notes:
FORMS:
Attaches directly to nouns: noun + だらけ
- {泥|どろ}だらけ (covered in mud)
- {傷|きず}だらけ (covered in scratches)
- {間違|まちが}いだらけ (full of mistakes)
- {血|ち}だらけ (covered in blood)

When modifying a noun, use の: {傷|きず}だらけの{車|くるま} (a car covered in scratches).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ～だらけ vs. ～まみれ: Both mean "covered in," but ～まみれ is limited to physical substances ({血|ち}まみれ, {汗|あせ}まみれ) and cannot be used with abstract nouns. ～だらけ works with both physical and abstract things ({間違|まちが}いだらけ, {借金|しゃっきん}だらけ).
- ～だらけ vs. ～ばかり: ～ばかり means "nothing but" without the negative nuance. ～だらけ always implies the situation is undesirable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傷|きず}だらけ (covered in scratches/wounds)
- {埃|ほこり}だらけ (covered in dust)
- {嘘|うそ}だらけ (full of lies)
- {借金|しゃっきん}だらけ (riddled with debt)
